plain.text: The LORD appeared to Abraham by the great trees of Mamre as he sat at his tent door in the heat of the day. Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. He hurried to meet them, bowed and urged them to rest while he brought water to wash their feet and something to eat. He hurried to Sarah to bake bread, chose a tender calf to be prepared, and served them curds, milk and the meat. He stood near them under a tree as they ate.

"Where is your wife Sarah?" they asked. "In the tent." The LORD said, "I will surely return to you about this time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son." Sarah was listening at the tent entrance. She was well past the age of having children, so she laughed to herself. The LORD asked, "Why did Sarah laugh? Is anything too hard for the LORD?" Sarah was afraid and denied it: "I did not laugh." But he said, "Yes, you did laugh."

As the men set out towards Sodom, the LORD said he would not hide from Abraham what he was about to do, since Abraham would become a great nation and teach his children to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just. The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah was great. Abraham approached and asked, "Will you sweep away the righteous with the wicked? What if there are fifty righteous people in the city? Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?" The LORD said he would spare it for fifty. Abraham, humbly and boldly, kept asking: forty-five? forty? thirty? twenty? ten? Each time the LORD agreed. "For the sake of ten, I will not destroy it." Then the LORD left, and Abraham returned home.

summary.bigIdea: Abraham welcomes surprise guests, Sarah laughs at God's promise, and Abraham pleads with God for Sodom.
points: Abraham shows warm hospitality to three visitors.
"Is anything too hard for the LORD?"
Abraham boldly asks God to spare Sodom for the sake of the righteous.
summary.reflection: Abraham kept asking God for mercy for others. Who could you pray for with that kind of persistence?
